overview: Poekilopleuron (meaning 'varied ribs') was a large carnivorous theropod from the Middle Jurassic of what is now Normandy, France, living approximately 168–165 million years ago. Described by Eudes-Deslongchamps in 1837–1838, it is estimated to have reached around 9 metres in length. It is known from a single partial skeleton—including forelimb, hind limb, and vertebral elements—found in the Calcaires de Caen Formation near Caen in Basse-Normandie.

Poekilopleuron belongs to Megalosauridae within the Tetanurae and is currently placed in the subfamily Eustreptospondylinae by some authorities; its PBDB record synonymises it partly with Megalosaurus. The original specimen was also lost during World War II bombing of Caen, leaving science dependent on earlier descriptions and casts. Its large forelimbs were an early observation that informed understanding of megalosauroid anatomy.

articles.title: Discovery and Naming
articles.body: Poekilopleuron bucklandii was described by Jacques-Amand Eudes-Deslongchamps in 1837–1838 from material excavated near Caen, Normandy. It was among the earliest large theropods to be scientifically described in France. The specimen was destroyed during Allied bombardment of Caen in World War II.

articles.title: Taxonomic History
articles.body: Poekilopleuron has had a complicated taxonomic history; material was at times referred to Megalosaurus, and the PBDB treats it as Megalosaurus (Poekilopleuron). It is currently regarded by many workers as a distinct genus within Megalosauridae, though its precise relationships within that family remain uncertain given the incompleteness of material.

articles.title: Anatomy
articles.body: Known elements include forelimb bones, vertebrae, pelvic fragments, and hind limb material. The forelimbs were notably robust, consistent with the megalosaurid body plan. Estimates of 9 metres in length make it one of the larger European theropods of the Jurassic, though this is approximate given the partial nature of the skeleton.

articles.title: Palaeoenvironment
articles.body: The Calcaires de Caen Formation represents shallow marine and coastal deposits of Bathonian age, suggesting Poekilopleuron lived in a near-coastal lowland environment. The French Jurassic was an archipelago landscape, and large theropods appear to have been apex predators across these island-studded seas.

record.description: Poekilopleuron bucklandii was a large theropod from the Calcaire de Caen of Normandy. Its partial skeleton was destroyed during the Second World War; casts, illustrations and a few separated elements preserve the evidence.
facts: The holotype included vertebrae, ribs, forelimbs and hindlimb parts but no complete skull.
Its megalosauroid affinity is likely, but exact placement and even continued diagnosability are debated.
Many later species once assigned to Poekilopleuron have been removed.
record.taxonomicStatus: historically valid but difficult to diagnose because the holotype was destroyed
